title: AI Engineering
description: A free, self-paced course in AI engineering: Python and maths, machine learning, deep learning, transformers and LLMs, then building, evaluating and shipping AI systems, with a Jupyter notebook for every lesson.

parts.name: Orientation
parts.desc: Set up your workbench and see the whole map before you start walking.

parts.name: Foundations
parts.desc: Python, numerical computing and the maths every later lesson leans on.

parts.name: Machine learning
parts.desc: How models learn from data, and how to tell whether they really did.

parts.name: Deep learning
parts.desc: Neural networks from first principles, then the same ideas in PyTorch.

parts.name: Transformers and LLMs
parts.desc: Attention, the transformer block, and how large language models are made.

parts.name: Building with LLMs
parts.desc: The core craft: APIs, prompts, reasoning models, retrieval, agents, context engineering and evaluation.

parts.name: Fine-tuning and inference
parts.desc: Change what a model knows and how it behaves, then make it fast and cheap to run: supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning and distillation, and the mechanics of LLM inference.

parts.name: Production
parts.desc: Serving, scaling, securing and extending AI systems in the real world.

parts.name: The wider field
parts.desc: The rest of AI beyond language models: search and planning, reinforcement learning, generative models, vision, time series and graphs, training at scale, and interpretability. Each lesson stands on its own, so take them in order or pick the ones your work needs.

parts.name: Mastery
parts.desc: System design, capstone projects, and turning skill into a career.
